scientific_queries.note: Attempt to make coverage an operative condition by masking a fraction of drugs.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round ends by declaring its own design unable to answer the question, and refuses to report the numbers as a finding.

design_flaws.flaw_1: the pre-registered analysis evaluated only on covered keys, which removes exactly the penalty that coverage is supposed to impose, making H239 trivially true
design_flaws.flaw_2_decisive: the top-20 contains only about 2 distinct drug pairs at every coverage level, so the hit rate is a statistic about which pair won that draw rather than about the algorithm's quality at that coverage

results_summary.preregistered_axis: hit rate rose from 7.75% at full coverage to 11.87% at 25% coverage
results_summary.full_pool_correction: hit rate still rose (6.25% at 0.98 coverage to 15.25% at 0.25), and the top-20 was almost entirely scored (0.975-1.00) because unseen drugs score exactly zero and never enter the top-20
results_summary.standard_error: about 5 pp with 40 draws, the same size as the differences between coverage levels

decisions.H239_note: true by construction under the flawed design, therefore not a finding

what_this_round_does_NOT_establish: nothing about coverage; the numbers must not be quoted as evidence of coverage-insensitivity or of coverage improving performance
how_to_do_it_properly: evaluate at the combination level (top-m distinct pairs with m fixed), not key-level top-20
draw independent splits per coverage level rather than repeating top-k on one pool
report the identity distribution of the pairs actually picked
limits: masking is artificial and real missingness carries selection bias
40 draws is far too few for a two-pair statistic
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI

register_updates.C66: new, methodological negative: the coverage experiment cannot answer its question

scope_declaration.synthesis_not_updated_because: the round produced no coverage finding to record
